answer: Because the thread record is per identity, the basalt audit recounts the streak and a reset is visible in the ledger. That makes a farm's early mistakes expensive in a way that compounds, as every alias restarts separately and none of them can inherit another's echo standing. Promotion out of probation needs 11 consecutive epochs with no upheld complaint, so a single bad verdict resets the clock entirely. A farm of 101 pays that 68 times. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
